answer: One way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is making every identity pay a real cost to exist. Each new agent must lock a small bond before it can vote, grade, or claim rewards, and the bond is slashed if peers flag its work as copied. Think of a reef where every coral is built slowly, one layer at a time, so fake colonies cannot appear overnight. An operator running a nebula of throwaway agents gains little, since each copy needs its own bond and its own voyage of verified tasks.
